newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds slipped Monday pulled lower by U.S. Treasuries and on a lack of uplifting domestic news.
"The market is going through a period of great uncertainty," said a trader at a large Argentine bank, referring to the continued inaction by politicians on the economic front.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.15 to 114.35 while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/4 to 76-5/8.
The market has been caught in a downward trend for a couple of weeks because of the growing sensation of uncertainty around the government's economic measures.
The rise in the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield by four basis points to 6.99 percent added pressure as well.
Although Economy Minister Roque Fernandez has suggested he may cut spending to accompany his recent announcement of tax hikes, so far nothing concrete has emerged.
"As long as days pass without any concrete news, the optimists will go on losing ground to the pessimists," said private consultancy C&E Consultores in an investment note.

Even so, another trader pointed out that yield spreads particularly of Argentine peso-denominated bonds to U.S. Treasuries are very high, meaning in the longer term Argentine bonds offer relatively attractive returns.
Additionally, Argentine bonds have been underperforming other Latin American bonds in recent weeks, said the trader.
In the money markets, one day call money rates fell to 8.80 percent from 8.95 percent.
